summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Amex nabs new risk chief
articles.description: The executive shuffle comes at a pivotal time for Amex, which was hit this month with regulator penalties over anti-money laundering compliance failures.

articles.title: FTC, states sue Toast over fees
articles.description: The agency and eight states allege that the point-of-sale services provider charges its restaurant clients and their customers hidden fees.

articles.title: Elavon pursues Paze, agentic commerce
articles.description: Mobile wallet Paze is “ready to do pilots,” said Wally Mlynarski, CEO of the U.S. Bank subsidiary.

articles.title: Will ditching the ‘honor all cards’ rule matter?
articles.description: Visa and Mastercard agreed to drop the standard in settling litigation with merchants, but the concession may not be much of a victory.

articles.title: Settling cross-border payments remains tough
articles.description: Global payments are moving faster, but local settlement remains a pain point for many companies, according to speakers on a Money20/20 panel.

articles.title: Visa adapts to tech innovations
articles.description: The card network’s fiscal 2026 results show it’s reaching beyond legacy payments paths to incorporate new technologies, offer new services and extend its global reach with more partners.

articles.title: Liability looms over AI shopping
articles.description: Some banks and other payment players lament how agentic commerce has steamrolled ahead without “rules of the road” for liability issues.

articles.title: Venmo results lift PayPal
articles.description: The digital payments processor is benefiting from its peer-to-peer payment tool business after cutting 2,000 employee jobs.
